subject: Atlas Health SLA / maintenance windows - proposed redlines and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@atlashealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial SLA asks and maintenance planning

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Atlas’ security and infra teams asked me to surface a few non-negotiable items we need addressed in the MSA/Order Form before we can move to procurement:

- Uptime target: 99.95% measured monthly across production region.
- Service credits: monthly credit equal to 5% of monthly invoice for each 0.05% below the target (capped at 50%).
- P1 response time: acknowledgement within 15 minutes, engineer engagement within 1 hour.
- Planned maintenance: windows must be published 14 days in advance for non-critical maintenance; no more than 4 planned maintenance events per quarter that affect production.
- Emergency maintenance: require post-event RCA within 72 hours.

Attached is a short SLO/ops request doc from Atlas’ side to make it concrete. We’ll need your legal team to confirm acceptable language. Also looping in our contracts inbox (contracts@atlashealth.com) for visibility.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate or propose alternate wording? We’re aiming to get this into the MSA addendum this week.

Best,
Elena
Director, Platform Reliability
Atlas Health
[Attachment: Atlas_SLO_Request.pdf]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-06T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks and maintenance planning

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and for the doc. Appreciate the timeline expectation. Quick read: we can meet much of this but need to align a few items with legal and ops (credit caps, measurement granularity, and P1 acknowledgment SLAs).

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to share a redline of the MSA/Order Form targeted at the items you listed (will include proposed language for credits and maintenance).
2) Ops sync: 30-minute call with our SRE lead to walk maintenance cadence and RCA timelines — propose Wed 11/8 10:00 PT.
3) DocuSign: if redlines are acceptable, we’ll send an MSA addendum + updated order form for signature.

Attaching a draft from our side for redlines so legal can start review: Redwood_Proposed_SLA_Redlines.docx. I’ll also loop in Laura from Legal and Marissa from SFDC-facing account ops to expedite.

Thanks — speak soon.

— Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_SLA_Redlines.docx]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlas Health SLA asks — need legal + ops suggestions

Team — forwarding Elena’s asks and our draft. High priority: Atlas wants 99.95% and very aggressive P1 timing. My read: we can be flexible on target and support cadence but need to tighten definitions (what counts as downtime, regional measurement, rolling maintenance treatment). Requests:

- Marissa: can you validate realistic maintenance cadence and proposed limits? Ops call Wed 11/8 10:00 PT is on my calendar.
- Ben: please provide suggested wording for measurement/aggregation (per-region vs global) and confirmation on RCA SLA (72 hours ok).
- Laura: need legal redlines for credits (formula and cap), and whether we can limit credit to a subset of services or require credit to be used as invoice offset only. Also advise on P1 acknowledgement vs engineer engagement wording.

Key items from our draft (summary):
- Measurement: 99.9% baseline for full-credit formula; 99.95% alternate proposal but credits capped at 30% of monthly invoice.
- Credits: step function with defined banding rather than linear 5% per 0.05% (simpler to administer).
- Maintenance: 14-day notice for non-emergency, up to 6 maintenance events/year that may affect production (ops prefers this to hard quarterly cap).
- RCA: 72 hours for preliminary RCA, 14 calendar days for full RCA.

Please reply with suggested language track-changes or call notes. I’ll consolidate and reply to Elena + contracts@atlashealth.com.

Thanks — Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas Health SLA asks — need legal + ops suggestions

Priyom — quick ops take (copied Ben for measurement detail, Laura for legal framing):

Operational suggestions (from SRE perspective):
- Measurement: define "Service Unavailable" as inability to process user requests due to Redwood runtime failures (exclude client-side errors, network outages outside our ASNs). Measure per-region; provide monthly availability as weighted average of region traffic.
- Target: recommend offering 99.9% as the standard enterprise tier and 99.95% as a purchasable premium (adds cost). If Atlas requires 99.95% without premium, recommend a credit cap of 30% monthly invoice.
- Credits: propose banded credits: 99.9%-99.95% = 5% credit; 99.8%-99.9% = 10%; <99.8% = 30% (cap). Easier for billing and ops.
- Maintenance events: ops is comfortable with up to 6 maintenance windows/year that may affect production if we schedule them with 14 days’ notice. For emergency maintenance (security patch, critical regressions) we will notify ASAP and provide full RCA within 14 days; preliminary notice within 24 hours post-event.
- P1 timelines: acknowledgement within 15 minutes is tough for global customers; we can commit to acknowledgement within 30 minutes and Engineer engagement within 1 hour. If Atlas insists on 15-minute engineer engagement, suggest a premium SOC add-on.

I made inline suggestions in the attached tracked-changes doc to speed legal review.

— Marissa
Sr. Director, Customer Solutions
[Attachment: msaredline_track_changes.docx]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@atlashealth.com>, contracts@atlashealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks and maintenance planning — consolidated proposal

Hi Elena and Atlas contracts team — thanks for the patience. We reviewed your asks with Ops and Legal and want to propose the following consolidated approach so procurement can move forward this week: 

Summary of agreed / proposed items:
- Availability: Redwood will offer 99.95% as a premium service tier (Order Form line item). Enterprise default is 99.9%.
- Credits: banded credit model (99.9%–99.95% -> 5% credit; 99.8%–99.9% -> 10%; <99.8% -> 30%) with an overall cap equal to 30% of the monthly invoice for the impacted service. Credits are applied as invoice offsets; not refundable.
- Measurement: availability measured per-region (production region defined in Order Form), excluding third-party network outages and scheduled maintenance windows. Monthly measurement period.
- P1 support: acknowledgement within 30 minutes, engineer engagement within 1 hour. 15-minute engagement available as a paid SOC add-on.
- Maintenance: 14 days’ notice for planned maintenance that may affect production; up to 6 planned events/year that may impact availability. Emergency maintenance: Redwood will notify as soon as practicable and provide preliminary RCA within 72 hours and full RCA within 14 calendar days.

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached Order_Form_v3.pdf reflecting the premium 99.95% line item and credit caps.
2) If Atlas approves these updates, we’ll circulate an MSA addendum (DocuSign link included) for signature and update the HubSpot deal record.
3) Ops call is still on for Wed 11/8 10:00 PT — Marissa will run through the maintenance cadence and measurement semantics; Ben will share metric dashboards.

If this looks acceptable, please reply with confirmation and any redlines to the order form so we can move to signature.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Order_Form_v3.pdf]
